acme_integration: Hi team — we're hitting a 415 when trying to stream results from the rerank endpoint. We switched our client to use SSE (Content-Type: text/event-stream) to try to get live updates, but the call just returns `415 Unsupported Media Type` and no payload. Anyone seen this?

oliver_support: Thanks for flagging — can you paste the exact curl (sanitized token) you're using and the response body?

acme_integration: Here's a trimmed repro:
```bash
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
     -H 'Content-Type: text/event-stream' \
     -d '{"queries":["best article about scaling inference"],"candidates":[{"id":"1","text":"doc a"},{"id":"2","text":"doc b"}]}' \
     https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank
```
Response (headers only):
```
HTTP/1.1 415 Unsupported Media Type
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"unsupported content-type: text/event-stream"}
```

oliver_support: OK that's helpful. Short answer: rerank is a synchronous JSON-only endpoint — it doesn't support SSE/streaming. If you send text/event-stream the API rejects it (hence the 415).

acme_integration: Ah — the docs aren't explicit about that, they just show streaming examples for generation. Our client assumed all endpoints accept SSE.

oliver_support: Understood. Workaround: send Content-Type: application/json and you'll get a standard JSON response (not streamed). Example of a working request:
```bash
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"queries":["best article about scaling inference"],"candidates":[{"id":"1","text":"doc a"},{"id":"2","text":"doc b"}]}' \
     https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank
```
The response will be a single JSON object with scores.

acme_integration: Got it — switching client now. Quick follow: are there any candidate limits or body-size constraints we should watch for? We were also getting weird low/identical scores when we tried a large candidate list.

jayden_sre: For limits — rerank expects up to 100 candidates per request (recommend <50 for latency). If you send several hundred you'll hit payload limits or timeouts. Also ensure you send candidates as an array of objects with text fields, not newline-delimited strings — malformed inputs can produce degenerate scores.

acme_integration: The client was building candidates as a newline-joined blob, that may be the root cause of the scoring oddity. We'll normalize to an array.

oliver_support: One more thing: please verify you aren't chunking the body with Transfer-Encoding: chunked while claiming text/event-stream. Some HTTP clients set streaming headers automatically and upstream proxies reject the combination. Using application/json with a normal content-length is the safest.

acme_integration: Thanks — switching both content-type and payload shape now.

oliver_support: If you want, paste a sample of your normalized request and we'll sanity-check. Also looping in tina_ml to consider improving the error message/documentation: @tina_ml can we return a clearer `unsupported streaming` error on rerank and add a docs note? :thinking:

deploy-bot: Notice: Support thread 1898765432 escalated to ML team (tina_ml) by oliver_support.


.tina_ml: Adding to backlog — agree we should make the error friendlier and include explicit non-streaming note in the rerank docs. For the customer, we can also add an e2e sample showing arrays and recommended batch sizes.

acme_integration: Appreciate the quick help — switching things now, will report back. :thumbsup:

oliver_support: Follow-up: if you still need incremental scoring semantics (near-real-time), consider sending smaller batches frequently or building a websocket-based prefetch layer that calls rerank per-batch — but no native SSE on rerank currently.

acme_integration: Understood, thanks. We'll test and re-open if anything else pops up. :pray:
